minutes.headline: Finance Committee kept its FY21 schedule; town manager will rebuild the budget on cautious revenue and postponed hires
minutes.summary: The committee met remotely under the governor's COVID-19 order. The town manager said revenue and state aid are unknown, so she would build FY21 conservatively, postpone new positions and push back capital projects. Members also discussed inviting state legislators, the town hiring freeze, and School Committee pay for hourly staff. The only vote was to adjourn.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee will keep its existing budget calendar, with only the sewer, general government and unclassified hearings left before the public hearing.
The town manager said FY21 revenue and state aid are unknown, and she would build the budget cautiously, starting from the FY20 state aid number.
She plans to postpone new positions and some capital projects so less tax revenue goes to capital and more to operations.
Members agreed to try to invite state legislators or their aides; a member will draft the request.
The School Committee voted to keep paying cafeteria and extended day staff from revolving funds, with no transfer needed yet.

why_it_matters: The FY21 budget is being built on cautious revenue, so postponed hires and capital projects could change which town services and projects are funded in the coming tax year.
Paying hourly school staff from revolving funds keeps the cost off the school operating budget for now, but a transfer may be needed if the emergency continues.

The remaining departmental hearings (sewer, general government, unclassified) before the public hearing.
